PRESCHOOL · AGE 3 · CLASS 8 MAGIC GAME

Magic Fruit Basket

Eight fruits, one basket and a little bit of magic. Meet the fruits, fill the basket, find them, count them — then hunt for real fruit in your kitchen. Grown-ups read the words; little ones do the tapping.

No scores, no timers — just fruit play.

STEP 2 · MEET THE FRUITS

Eight fruits are waiting to say hello.

Tap a fruit to hear its name spoken out loud. Say it together — then tap the next one. Which fruit do you have at home?

The names are spoken by your device’s friendly screen voice. The words on each card are the text alternative — read them together any time.

STEP 3 · FILL THE BASKET

Put every fruit in the magic basket.

Drag a fruit into the basket — or tap the fruit, then tap the basket. Watch it land with a gentle pop!

The basket is empty.

Tap a fruit below, then tap the basket. (Dragging works too.)

STEP 4 · FIND THE FRUIT

Find the fruit.

You read the words, your child taps the fruit. A miss is just another look.

Tap the apple!

Tap the pineapple!

Tap the watermelon!

Tap the grapes!

Tap the strawberry!

STEP 5 · COUNT THE FRUITS

Count them out loud.

Point at each fruit and count: one… two… three… then tap the number you said.

How many apples?

How many bananas?

How many bunches of grapes?

How many strawberries?

STEP 6 · OFF-SCREEN PLAY

The kitchen fruit hunt.

The magic continues away from the screen. Pick one of these — five minutes is plenty — and let your child lead.

Basket hunt

  • Take a real basket or bowl and hunt the kitchen together: an apple, a banana, whatever fruit lives with you. Every find goes in with a proud “plop!” — just like the game.

Guess my fruit

  • Hide a fruit behind your back and give clues: “It is yellow and curved like a smile!” Let your child guess — then swap roles and let them be the tricky one.

Count the fruit bowl

  • Pour out the fruit bowl and count it together: how many apples? How many altogether? Real fruit beats flashcards every time.

One safety word for this game: wash fruits before touching mouths, grown-ups do all the cutting, whole grapes are cut small for little mouths, and everyone sits down while eating. Tasting is for real food a grown-up has checked — never anything you find on the floor.

STEP 7 · ACTIVITY COMPLETE

The basket is magic — and so are you!

You met eight fruits, filled the basket, found them hiding and counted them out loud. Whether you played one step or all of them, that was real learning — and there was never a score to worry about. The real basket in your kitchen is waiting for its next fruit hunt.

FOR GROWN-UPS

How the magic works.

This game uses the eight fruit illustrations from the Fruits & Vegetables class — the same pictures your child may already know from their flashcard pages. Tapping a fruit speaks its name with your device’s built-in screen voice; if your device is quiet or you prefer it, the name is always written right there on the card, and saying it in your own voice is even better.

Fill the Basket works by tapping (tap the fruit, then tap the basket) or by dragging, so both big-desktop mice and small-tablet fingers are welcome. Nothing is graded: the counter on the basket only counts how many fruits have landed, and misses simply mean another try.

Playing side by side beats playing alone at this age. Ask “which one is your favorite?” — and let the kitchen finish the lesson.
